meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Twenty-five minutes, Hale, and I have a call at 4:40. Owen found out he had a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Before we go any further, who decided on that zero, and was Owen heard first?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what that zero is based on.

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
That's a file history, Hale, not a hearing, and your own procedure says you speak to the student first, so did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2. Seventeen-year-olds put a half-remembered line in quotation marks all the time, Hale, and that's a sloppy citation, not proof of anything.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
That's 4.4. I want that in writing tonight, nothing on his file, and nobody in his class hearing a word of it. Before I agree to Thursday, Hale, who else has seen this so far?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged that the zero was entered before I was contacted, and you offered Owen a supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that offer in writing, a written guarantee that nothing goes on Owen's file and nothing is said in front of his class, and a full answer as to who else has seen this matter. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her fallback position, with your procedure 4.4 offer meeting her demand that this stay off his record and stay quiet, but she had not yet accepted Thursday; she still wants the offer in writing tonight, a guarantee that nothing goes on file or reaches his class, and to know who else has seen it, and that private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record is the fair outcome, which you were one exchange away from with time still on her clock.
What moved her: Owning the early zero in one sentence and then giving her a quotation she could search in the play herself, because it was specific, tied to Owen's work and checkable without trusting you.
What cost ground: You never answered whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in, which left her a live procedure point to stand on while she held off agreeing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placing the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 the night before it was due landed right on that kind of night, which is why she went short and straight to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she called the line a sloppy citation, show her that it is not a garbled version of any real line in Hamlet and answer whether Owen was heard first, before offering the rewrite.
